items.title: Cedar Walton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Uh-huh. Was that the Elvin, McCoy, Jimmy Grier band? [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah. Uh-hm. That's who it was.

ctx.x: [laughs] Sometime. He hadn't gotten to that point yet they would play that long.
Uh-huh. Was that the Elvin, McCoy, Jimmy Grier band?

Yeah. Uh-hm. That's who it was. And it was just very exciting. We played opposite them uh, in uh, Lincoln Center, the original Lincoln Center up on 64th Street – Alice Tully Hall. I remember one night … they had a long bar where we were waiting and we could hear them. They had a, uh, uh, acoustic sound system that they uh, piped into the bar. We could hear Trane's group and uh, and uh, he uh, sort of opened for us as uh, as we called it. I hadn't, that term hadn't uh, really, uh, surfaced yet: opening act. Not in…
